turns.t: Doctor, it won't stop bleeding. I've been spitting blood into the sink for ages, sure look at the state of this towel.
Right, let's sort you out. Sit here. Where is the bleeding coming from?
From where the tooth came out this morning. Bottom left, the back one. The dentist said it'd stop by lunchtime.
It was two hours before he'd even tell me, Doctor. He's stubborn.
Ah, Aoife, would you stop. It's only been two hours, I'd say. Maybe a bit more.
It's three hours, Dad. I looked at the clock when we left the house. I've been holding that towel since.
So two hours, or three, somewhere in that region. We'll say two to three hours of bleeding. Nurse, can you get the numbers please?
Of course. Mr Gallagher, just pop that cuff on your arm. Hold the gauze in your mouth too.
Blood pressure is 142 over 88. Pulse 96. Temperature 36.9 degrees.
Oxygen saturation is 98 percent and respiratory rate is 16.
Thanks. Is it dripping, or an ooze?
A steady ooze, doctor. Bright red. When I take the gauze out it fills right up again.
Any pain with it, or is it mostly the bleeding?
The jaw is sore. A dull, throbbing thing. Not terrible, but I'd say it's getting worse since breakfast.
Do you feel faint or light-headed at all?
No, not at all. I'm grand. I just hate the taste of it.
Any bleeding from anywhere else? Nose, gums, bruises coming up?
No, nothing else. Only the mouth.
He gets bruises easily though, Doctor. Always has. It's the tablets.
Which tablets are those?
The warfarin. 5 mg every evening, for the heart. I never miss it.
For the irregular heartbeat, that's the atrial fibrillation?
That's the one. About four years now. And yer man, the dentist, didn't even ask me if I'd stopped it.
Did you tell him you take it?
I did, I did. He said grand, grand, and went ahead.
Okay. Do you have any allergies to medicines, latex, anything?
None at all. Never had a bother.
Does anyone in the family have bleeding problems or clotting problems?
Not really. Granddad Gallagher had a stroke, years ago. Dad's dad, I mean.
Thanks. Do you smoke, or drink?
I smoke about ten a day. And a few pints at the weekend, sure what else would you do.
Let me look at the mouth. Open wide, please.
The socket at the bottom left is oozing steadily, and there's no clot sitting in it. The gum around it is not swollen.
Is that bad?
It's a socket that hasn't clotted, which on warfarin is not unusual. I can't rule out that your warfarin level is running too high.
So is it the warfarin that's doing it?
Possibly. I can't rule out a high level yet, or just a slow-to-clot socket. That's why I'd like to order an INR blood test now.
I can do that straight away, Doctor. I'll draw it while he's sitting there.
And I'd like a full blood count as well, to check how much blood he's lost.
Will I need a transfusion?
I doubt it. First, bite firmly on this fresh gauze for twenty minutes without peeking. No rinsing or spitting.
No peeking. Right. I'll do my best.
I'll keep an eye on the clock this time, Doctor.
Good woman. We'll watch him here until the results are back.
